summary: The 3D floor view (floor_3d.js) no longer invents a four-sided perimeter wall for a floor with no authored wall segments -- it now extrudes exactly what the operator drew, so an area with no outer wall simply shows a bare slab in 3D, matching the 2D plan. Separately, camera markers in the 3D view now gain parity with the 2D plan's unread-notification indicator: a camera with unread alerts shows a severity-coloured count badge (a billboard sprite, always facing the camera and drawn through walls, 99+ capped) and, on the floor beneath it, a two-wave pulse in the alert's severity colour matching the beacon already used on the fleet-map building markers. In the stacked multi-floor view the badge appears on every floor so an alert a storey down stays visible, but only the active/non-dimmed floor pulses, bounding the motion. The unread count/severity is now part of the 3D scene's rebuild signature so a new alert appears or clears immediately without any other input changing. Also hardened 3D scene teardown so it no longer disposes the shared module-level sprite geometry (three.js sprites share one geometry instance; disposing it broke every sprite created after the first).
compatibility: Frontend-only, no API/schema change. Existing floor plans with no authored walls now render as a bare 3D slab instead of a boxed room -- a deliberate, user-visible correction (an outer wall must be drawn to appear in 3D); any floor with authored wall segments is unaffected. The notification badge/pulse is additive and reads the same notifByCam data BuildingFloorView already fetches for the 2D plan -- no new endpoint, no behavior change for floors/cameras with zero unread notifications.
